$comment: Plugin configuration for benchmark jobs, in two layers.
'seed' profiles are baked into the image by build_template.py: a real
package_manager install from origin/store, so the template carries its own
provenance rather than a claim about it. Changing one means rebuilding.
'runtime' profiles are deltas the entrypoint applies to that seed when a
container starts. They are what a job names, and they need no rebuild --
which is the point, because comparing plugin sets is the experiment.
A runtime profile's 'remove' list is the interesting direction: the seed
carries everything, and a profile asks what the agent can do without.

bench.description: Essentials minus interactive-only pieces, web search, and SQL. Search is forbidden by task constraints, so offering it invites a violation the oracle then punishes; sql_query drew zero calls across every run recorded so far. Both cost prompt tokens in every request to sit unused.

bench-full.description: The seed exactly as built, web search and SQL included. Kept so a run can be reproduced against the tool set used before those two were dropped.

no-script.description: Drops run_script and validate. Tests the hypothesis that the script-and-verify pair costs more tokens than it earns once no approval dialog can refuse a shell command anyway.

no-validate.description: Keeps run_script, drops validate alone, to separate the cost of scripting from the cost of checking.

no-subagents.description: Drops delegation. Isolates whether subagent spawning helps or merely multiplies context.

lean.description: File and shell work only: no scripting, no delegation, no search tools.
